title: Open cloze: the lost data
instructions: Escribí UNA palabra gramatical en cada hueco.
text: If we [1] made a backup yesterday, we would not have lost the data. Now I wish I [2] been more careful. From now on I will save my work every day, and I will keep a copy [3] case the computer crashes. I will not change anything [4] I have tested it first. As long as we follow this plan, we [5] not lose data again.

pat: yesterday + would not have lost → Third Conditional: If we had made.
would nunca va en la cláusula if: If we had made.
items.e: Third: If + had + participio.

pat: arrepentimiento del pasado → wish + past perfect: wish I had been.
items.e: I wish + had been (arrepentimiento).

pat: la expresión fija es in case (por si acaso).
items.e: in case = por si acaso.

pat: if daría el sentido contrario; 'no cambiaré nada a menos que lo haya probado': unless.
items.e: not ... unless = a menos que ya lo haya probado.

pat: As long as + presente simple → First Conditional: we will not lose.
items.e: as long as (condición posible) + will en la cláusula principal.

title: Open cloze: wishes and regrets
instructions: Escribí UNA palabra gramatical en cada hueco.
text: I wish I [1] more time to learn new tools, but my job is very busy. If only my manager [2] understand how much work there is! If I [3] the manager, I would hire two more people. Last year I did not ask for a raise. If I had asked, I [4] have received one, and I would not [5] so stressed now.

pat: después de wish se retrocede un tiempo: wish + pasado simple (had).
items.e: Presente → Past Simple (had).

pat: para quejas sobre otra persona: wish + would. will no se usa después de wish y could es habilidad.
items.e: Queja sobre otra persona → would.

pat: Second Conditional: If I were (o was); am sería First y would no va en la cláusula if.
items.e: Second: If I were the manager.

pat: If I had asked (past perfect) → Third Conditional: would/might/could have received.
items.e: Third: would/might/could have + participio.

pat: después de would not va el verbo base: would not be.
items.e: would not BE so stressed now (resultado en el presente).

title: Multiple choice cloze: the server crash
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta para cada hueco.
text: If the server [1] down, users cannot open the website. Yesterday it crashed and we lost some data. If we [2] a backup, we would not have lost it. The manager says: "If we see the problem again, we will change providers." I wish it [3] never happened. As long as we [4] the new plan, everything will be fine. I will also keep a copy of the files in case the system [5] again.

items.e: Zero: hecho general.

will go: Zero Conditional (hecho general): presente en las dos cláusulas. will no va acá.
went: pasado simple sería Second Conditional; users cannot open es un hecho general: goes.

items.e: Pasado imaginario → Past Perfect.

made: yesterday + would not have lost → Third Conditional: had made.
would make: would nunca va en la cláusula if: If we had made.

items.e: I wish it had never happened.

has: Present Perfect no va después de wish; arrepentimiento del pasado → past perfect: had never happened.
would: wish + would es para quejas o cambios futuros; sobre algo que ya pasó: had never happened.

items.e: as long as + Present Simple.

will follow: will no va después de as long as: as long as we follow.
are following: are following es gramatical (acción en curso); la estructura estándar de este ejercicio es el presente simple: follow.

items.altnote: Correcta con aviso: are following es gramatical (acción en curso). La estructura estándar de as long as es el presente simple (follow); en el examen, esa es la que se espera.

items.e: in case + Present Simple.

will crash: will no va después de in case: in case the system crashes.
would crash: would no va después de in case (con 'I will keep' va presente): in case the system crashes.

title: Multiple choice cloze: a delayed project
instructions: Elegí la opción correcta para cada hueco.
text: Our project was delayed. If we [1] the requirements more carefully at the start, we could have finished on time. To be honest, I wish we [2] more people in the team. If only the client [3] stop changing the requirements every week! Unless the client [4] the design this week, we will not finish on time. [5], we should have clearer contracts in future.

items.e: Pasado imaginario → If + Past Perfect.

analysed: could have finished (Third Conditional) pide past perfect en if: had analysed.
would have analysed: would have nunca va en la cláusula if: If we had analysed.
would analyse: would nunca va en la cláusula if: If we had analysed.

items.e: Presente → Past Simple (had).

would have: would have no va después de wish; wish + pasado simple para el presente: had.
have: después de wish se retrocede un tiempo: wish + pasado simple (had).
could have: could have no va después de wish para tener algo; wish + pasado simple: had.

items.e: Queja sobre otro → If only + would.

will: will no se usa después de if only; para quejas sobre otros: would.
did: did + stop no existe; para pedir un cambio en otros: would stop.
had: had + stop no existe; para pedir un cambio en otros: would stop.

items.e: Unless + afirmativo, Present Simple.

doesn't approve: unless ya es negativo (= if not); no lleva otra negación: Unless the client approves.
will approve: will no va después de unless: Unless the client approves.
approved: la frase habla del futuro (this week, will not finish): presente simple, approves.

items.e: Conclusión final del texto.

First: First abre una secuencia; esto cierra el texto: In conclusion.
Lastly: Lastly = por último; ordena una lista, y acá se concluye: In conclusion.
Then: Then = luego (secuencia); acá se concluye: In conclusion.

title: Gapped text: the risky migration
instructions: Cinco oraciones fueron eliminadas del texto. Elegí de la lista (A-H) la que encaja en cada hueco. Hay TRES oraciones que sobran.
text: Marta manages a small team of developers. Last month, the company asked her team to move all its data to a new cloud provider. [1] If everything goes well, the change will save a lot of money. However, the process is risky. Two years ago, a similar project failed because the tests had not been completed. [2] Marta says that if they had planned it better, they would have avoided those problems. This time, she wants to be careful. [3] The team will not start the migration unless every test passes. [4] As a result, the launch has been postponed by two weeks. Some managers are unhappy about it. Personally, Marta believes it is the right decision. [5] She wishes the company had listened to her advice earlier.
bank: The company hopes to finish the work by the end of the year.
It was a very expensive mistake.
She has asked the directors for more time and more tests.
The first results, however, have not been good enough.
A failed launch would be much more expensive than a delay.
Marta studied law before becoming a manager.
The migration finished yesterday without any problems.
Next year the company will open offices in three new countries.

a: The company hopes to finish the work by the end of the year.
items.e: Introduce el plan; 'the change' en la oración siguiente se refiere a la migración.

a: It was a very expensive mistake.
items.e: Comenta el proyecto fallido; Marta lo retoma con un condicional.

a: She has asked the directors for more time and more tests.
items.e: Muestra cómo Marta 'wants to be careful' antes de la regla del equipo.

a: The first results, however, have not been good enough.
items.e: Es la causa; 'As a result' introduce la consecuencia (el retraso).

a: A failed launch would be much more expensive than a delay.
items.e: Justifica la opinión de Marta (Second Conditional) antes de su arrepentimiento.

title: Email de deploy
instructions: Leé el mensaje y elegí la respuesta correcta.
text:
To: Dev team
Subject: Deployment tonight
Hi team, if the tests pass this afternoon, we will deploy the new version tonight. Please don't merge anything else unless I tell you. Take a copy of your local branch in case something goes wrong. Thanks, Nora.

o: Wait for Nora's permission before merging
items.a: Wait for Nora's permission before merging
items.e: 'don't merge anything else unless I tell you'.

Deploy the version right now: Nora dice que se hará el deploy esta noche y solo si los tests pasan esta tarde.
Delete their local branches: pide hacer una copia (take a copy) de la rama local por si algo sale mal, no borrarla.

title: Aviso de seguridad
instructions: Leé el aviso y elegí la respuesta correcta.
text:
SECURITY NOTICE
If you receive an email asking for your password, do not answer it. Forward it to security@company.com in case other employees receive it too. Remember: IT will never ask you for your password.

items.q: What should employees do with a suspicious email?
o: Forward it to the security address
items.a: Forward it to the security address
items.e: 'Forward it to security@company.com'.

Answer it quickly: el aviso dice do not answer it.
Give their password to IT: el aviso dice que IT nunca pide la contraseña.

title: Post-mortem: the lost orders
instructions: Leé el texto y elegí la respuesta correcta para cada pregunta.
text:
Last Friday, the payments system stopped working for three hours. According to the report, the cause was a mistake made by a junior developer, Iván. He had run a script on the production database instead of the test database. If he had checked the server name, he would have noticed the problem immediately.
The team reacted quickly. As soon as they saw the error, they restored a backup. Unfortunately, the backup was two days old, so some customers lost their last orders. If the team had kept more recent copies, the loss would have been much smaller. Therefore, the company has decided to make backups every hour.
Iván feels terrible. "I wish I had read the screen more carefully," he says. "If only I had asked a colleague to review the script first!" His manager, however, does not blame him. "Anyone could have done the same," she says. "We will only improve if we learn from our mistakes. From now on, no one will touch the production database unless a second person approves the change."

o: A script run on the wrong database
items.a: A script run on the wrong database
items.e: 'run a script on the production database instead of the test database'.

A hardware breakdown: la causa fue un script ejecutado por error, no una falla de hardware.
A missing backup: había un backup (de dos días); el problema fue que estaba viejo.

items.q: How old was the backup the team restored?
items.e: 'the backup was two days old'.

One hour: una hora es la nueva frecuencia de backups, no la edad del backup restaurado.
One week: el backup tenía dos días, no una semana.

items.q: Why did some customers lose orders?
items.e: 'the backup was two days old, so some customers lost their last orders'.

Iván deleted them on purpose: fue un error (mistake), no algo a propósito.
The manager cancelled them: no se dice que el manager cancelara pedidos; el backup era viejo.

o: Not asking a colleague to review the script
items.a: Not asking a colleague to review the script
items.e: 'If only I had asked a colleague to review the script first!'.

Not deleting the backup: lo que lamenta es no haber pedido a un colega que revisara el script.
Not leaving the company: no habla de irse de la empresa.

o: Nobody will use the test database
Changes to production will need a second person's approval
items.a: Changes to production will need a second person's approval
items.e: 'no one will touch the production database unless a second person approves'.

Nobody will use the test database: la regla es sobre la base de producción, no sobre la de test.
Backups will be made weekly: la empresa decidió hacer backups cada hora, no semanales.

title: Testing in production
instructions: Leé el texto y elegí la respuesta correcta.
text: Some teams argue that if a system is not tested in real conditions, its problems will only appear when users arrive. That is why some companies run experiments with a small percentage of real users before a full launch. However, critics point out that this practice is acceptable only provided that failures cannot cause serious damage. A photo-sharing app, for example, might test a new button in production; a bank, on the other hand, would think twice unless it had a safe way to undo any change. If more companies had followed this cautious approach, several well-known outages might have been avoided.

items.q: According to critics, when is testing in production acceptable?
o: When failures cannot cause serious damage
When the company is very large
items.a: When failures cannot cause serious damage
items.e: 'acceptable only provided that failures cannot cause serious damage'.

When the company is very large: el tamaño de la empresa no es la condición; es que los fallos no causen daño grave.
When users complain: no se menciona que los usuarios se quejen como condición.
When there is no backup: sin backup sería más riesgoso, no aceptable.

items.q: What would a bank need before testing in production?
o: A safe way to undo any change
items.a: A safe way to undo any change
items.e: 'unless it had a safe way to undo any change'.

More users: el texto no habla de tener más usuarios; habla de poder deshacer cambios.
A new button: un botón nuevo es el ejemplo de la app de fotos, no lo que necesita un banco.
Fewer developers: no se habla de cantidad de desarrolladores.
